title: Micro-result scaffold: weekly synthesis & sprinting notes
content:
Context: quick personal synthesis for the two-week cadence. Aim is to track outcome-level progress (not tasks), surface blockers, and capture small experiments to keep momentum. Treat as lightweight: ~10–15 min at end of week.

Top-level outcomes (quarter):
- O1: Reduce average end-to-end gen latency by 18% for 1k seq workloads (measured as P95 client-perceived)
- O2: Increase throughput per GPU by 22% via batching and caching improvements
- O3: Ship two production-safe quantization presets for mid-size models

This doc: biweekly slice for 2026-02-24 → 2026-03-02 (notes, signals, micro-decisions).

Signals this sprint (what the data actually said)
- Latency: P95 dropped from 420ms → 370ms for the BAU test harness across canary traffic. Roughly -12% (short of 18% goal).
- Throughput: baseline batch-stealing heuristic produced +14% throughput on synthetic bench, but regressions in tail latency for short sequences (~<128) spiked 5–7%.
- Cost: perf changes imply ~8% lower token-cost on batch-oriented workloads; token-cost for small requests unchanged.
- Releases: PR #678 merged (baseline batch manager change). Canary rollout to 10% traffic started 2026-02-27; no incidents logged.

What I shipped / experimented
- Small experiment: aggressive prefix-KV caching for repeated prompt families (config toggle). Shows 20–35% reduction on synthetic repeat traffic.
- Tuned kernel scheduling weights for CUDA kernels (local bench). Good improvements for long sequences, slightly worse for short ones.
- Wrote a short eval harness (scripts/eval/biweek-latency.sh) to compare P50/P95 across client patterns.

Open questions / unresolved risks
- Is the tail latency spike acceptable for our short-seq customers? If we keep the new batching heuristic, we may need per-customer routing rule to fallback to low-batching mode.
- Do we have enough telemetry to attribute regressions to kernel scheduling vs queueing? Current traces are high-level; need per-kernel timing in prod.
- Does the caching config increase memory pressure on multi-tenant nodes? Early canary suggests small bump but need 24h observation.

Decisions to make next sprint
- If short-seq P95 > 200ms regression on any region for 3 consecutive hours, rollback batch-heuristic for that region (rollback runbook draft below).
- Add a canary metric for per-request kernel time (low overhead sampling).
- Prioritize a fallback policy in the router (per-tenant low-batch tag) vs fixing heuristics immediately.

Mini runbook/rollback (for myself)
- Slack @sre-oncall + create incident stub (use template INC-ops-small-tail).
- Roll canary down to 2% traffic in region via console → rollout → scale to previous snapshot.
- Re-run biweek-latency.sh against canary snapshot and compare kernel timings.

Weekly checklist (things to actually do during short slot)
- [x] Run biweek-latency.sh on canary vs prod baseline (done 2026-02-26)
- [x] Collect memory/caching metrics (heap/cached-kv counts) — initial pass done
- [ ] Add per-kernel timing probe (low overhead sampling) — dependent on infra slot
- [ ] Draft router fallback policy and test locally with simulated tenants
- [ ] Sync w/ Kara on rollout gating criteria (15m sync)

Notes-to-self (freeform)
- Keep narrative focused on outcomes when writing updates to PMs; avoid deep infra jargon in the top summary.
- When I document the fallback policy, include a concrete example tenant with thresholds — makes decisions easier for PMs.
- Remember: small wins on caching are cumulative; prioritize safety and observability first.

Retro: what went well
- Quick bench → deploy loop was short this sprint (PR to canary under 24h).
- Collaboration: Kara helped debug a scheduling mismatch in the local bench that would have misled the canary.

Retro: what to improve
- Need automated smoke test for short-seq tail before canary (this would have caught the small latency spike).
- My runbook was too conceptual; add explicit CLI commands and links.

Micro goals for next two weeks (clear, testable)
- G1: Implement low-overhead kernel sampling and collect 72h of data (pass = >100k sampled requests across regions).
- G2: Add router fallback flag and run staged simulation against 3 tenant profiles (pass = simulated regressed P95 < 200ms for short seq profile).
- G3: Author a one-pager for PMs outlining tradeoffs and a recommended shipping plan (pass = reviewed by Kara + PM).

Estimated timebox (realistic)
- Kernel probe: 2–3 days (prototype) + 4 days infra review + 2 days roll
- Router flag: 3 days prototype + 2 days integration tests
- One-pager: 1 day + 30m review

Personal notes / heuristics
- Prioritize observability when changing scheduling/batching; small regressions are easier to detect & rollback with good telemetry.
- When blocked, move to a tiny experiment that yields signal quickly (e.g., toggle cache on a synthetic tenant).
